$schema-note: Canonical surface-class routing (the drift detector, machine-readable). Every in-scope repo wears ONE of two type classes by JOB (not plumbing): 'editorial' (marketing/brand) or 'app' (product). One io navy+gold palette everywhere via tokens.css. The consumer drift-guard reads this to ENFORCE that a repo loads only the font families approved for its class, so the standard can't be violated silently. Prose + rationale live in the README and docs/ASTER_FLEET_TYPE_STANDARD_2026-07-17.md.
ruling: Fleet Type & Design Standard (architect 2026-07-17) — two classes by job, one io navy+gold palette. Supersedes the D1 'io-canon / Plex-everywhere' reading. v0.3.1 (2026-07-19): declares two approved deviations (aster-sports scoped Barlow 'broadcast'; st-patricks R6 rem-lift) — additive, no class/family/scale value changed. v0.3.2 (2026-08-15): declares a THIRD approved deviation (aster-io scoped Bricolage/Geist 'night' front door) — additive, no class/family/scale value changed, and the editorial end-state for the rest of the surface is untouched. v0.4.0 (2026-08-16): RETIRES the 'night' deviation and replaces it with 'storefront'. The night front door was reverted on 2026-08-16 and night.css deleted, so that deviation had zero consumers and its scope string named a file that no longer exists. It is removed rather than repurposed: its approvedBy stamp (Frank 2026-08-15) approved Bricolage+Geist for a DARK front door that was withdrawn the next day, and carrying that stamp onto a different decision would make this file — the one artifact every repo reads to learn what is sanctioned — assert an approval that was never given. 'storefront' is a new deviation with its own scope, faces, rationale and date: aster-io's body face only, Instrument Serif and IBM Plex Mono unchanged. Removing 'night' NARROWS the allowlist (drops Bricolage Grotesque and Geist); verified safe — no stylesheet, link tag or component in any of the six repos renders either face. MINOR, not patch: auto-tag.yml defines a patch as having no design surface, and retiring/declaring approved font families is design surface. It is therefore HELD pending [release-approved] by design — the gate exists so a face change cannot ship by merely merging. v0.5.0 (2026-09-03): RETIRES the 'storefront' deviation, leaving aster-io with no scoped deviation at all. It is removed for the reason v0.4.0 removed 'night', and the evidence is the same shape: zero consumers, and a scope string naming files that no longer exist. Measured on all 14 live astersports.io routes on 2026-09-03 — Figtree appears in no element's font stack and no Figtree woff2 is ever fetched; the consumer declares it on --sans and then overrides that with var(--atk-ed-body) in product.css, so the body face rendered has been IBM Plex Sans throughout. The scope read '.ah — the astersports.io marketing surface (client/src/styles/home.css + register.css)'; `.ah` matched zero elements on every route and both it and home.css were deleted in aster-io #233. Retiring this NARROWS the allowlist (drops Figtree) — verified safe: no stylesheet, link tag or component in any of the six repos renders it, and aster-io's own follow-up removes the Google Fonts request in the same breath. Ruled by the owner, 2026-09-03: 'Retire storefront upstream and drop Figtree.' MINOR, not patch, and HELD pending [release-approved] for the same reason v0.4.0 was: retiring an approved font family is design surface.

aster-io.note: The firm's storefront — the Editorial reference implementation. The editorial end-state (Instrument Serif, IBM Plex Sans, IBM Plex Mono) now holds everywhere on this surface, with no scoped deviation: 'storefront' was retired in v0.5.0.

nova-select.note: Sales demo / showroom — classified by JOB (showcase), NOT by plumbing. It runs on real app components (app-style UI is expected); do NOT strip its demo richness toward a bare tool.

scopedDeviations.name: broadcast
scopedDeviations.scope: .bc-root — the Records + Livescore sports-broadcast surfaces only
scopedDeviations.note: A deliberate sports-broadcast aesthetic (src/styles/broadcast.css + inline .bc-* sites). Scoped via .bc-root; the rest of the Hub stays App-clean (Inter / IBM Plex Mono). A consumer drift-guard honoring this MUST allow the Barlow family set within this scope and continue to flag Barlow (or any non-App-clean face) anywhere OUTSIDE it.

aster-sports.note: Hub — flagship parent gateway, App-Store-bound, dense data. Half of the Hub<->App invariant (see invariants.hubAppPairing). Email-renderer literal hex is an approved exception (email clients can't use CSS vars). The Barlow 'broadcast' theme on Records/Livescore is an approved SCOPED deviation — see scopedDeviations.

aster-studio.note: Print Studio — a tool, whole repo App-clean per Frank (Join/Billing included). Money repo: token/type wiring is presentational only.

scale.note: html{font-size:112.5%} lifts the rem-based scale ~+12.5% for older-reader legibility on the parish site. The uniformSystem.scalePx values remain the MINIMUM floors AFTER the lift (post-lift body ~18px still clears the 17px readable floor); --parish-scale-* may bind rem-relative. A consumer drift-guard honoring this must NOT assert the absolute uniformSystem.scalePx verbatim against this surface's rendered px — it validates the post-lift result against the floors instead.

st-patricks-armonk.note: Adopts the App-clean SYSTEM (scale, weights, floors, mono, drift-guard) but keeps parish colors + Fraunces headings as the DECLARED, enforced deviation. In scope as of 2026-07-17 (was outOfScope under D1). Pending GitHub-ownership transfer — wiring PR may wait on access.

hubAppPairing.note: The Hub (parent gateway) and the program App are one continuous product — a user moving between them must feel ONE product. Their App-clean type/token resolved values MUST be identical; any divergence is a P0 finding. The consumer-side drift-guard enforces this pairing hardest.

outOfScope.aster-weather: Headless library, no UI/type surface. Excluded by design so the audit's coverage is provably complete (5 in-scope repos, weather out).

gateAmendment.resultVocabulary: Final/LIVE attached to a score or completed state (banned on invented data, ruling 1B).
gateAmendment.legitimate: Round names in schedule rows (Semifinal A, Final, Regional Finals — a matchup with time/court, no score) are legitimate tournament nomenclature, not results.
